newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Honda Philippines launches car, to hike output.
newsitem.headline: Honda Philippines launches car, to hike output.

text.p: Japan's Honda Motor Co said on Monday it would consider increasing its production capacity in the Philippines to cater to export markets as well as growing domestic demand.
"We are now considering an increase in our production capacity in this country to meet future demand," Nobuhiko Kawamoto, Honda president and chief executive officer, told reporters in Manila.
"At the same time, we are also studying the feasibility of exports of automobiles from this country," he said.
"The Philippines has definitely become a significant part of our Asian operations," he said.
Kawamoto, in an interview, declined to say how much Honda would invest to expand production capacity in the Philippines or what portion of its output was earmarked for exports.

The Honda chief was in Manila for the launch of a new 1.3 litre model. He said Honda would produce 10,000 of the new four-door City saloon cars annually but this could be done with existing production facilities.
"We think we can meet production targets for the City without much immediate additional investment," he said.
Honda Philippines officials said the firm's plant, south of Manila, had an annual production capacity of 24,000 units.
"The existing (assembly) line will be extended to meet the estimated demand of 14,000 to 16,000 units for Civic and Accord models plus 10,000 City cars," an official said.
Honda's launch of its third model comes soon after eight-month car sales figures showed it had displaced Toyota as the top-selling manufacturer in the Philippines.
Honda Philippines at present sells its Accord and Civic models, both of which are of 1,500 cc category.
Total car sales in the Philippines in the first eight months of the year rose by 25 percent to 58,382 units compared to 46,675 in the year-ago period.

In the January to August, 1996, period Honda had the biggest share of 13,704 units or 23 percent followed by Toyota with 12,968 units or 22 percent, Mitsubishi Motors with 16 percent and Nissan Motor Co with 13.7 percent.
Last year, Philippine car sales rose by 22 percent to 71,176. Honda was then in fourth position selling 11,673 cars, accounting for 16 percent of the market.
Toyota led in 1995 with 17,107 vehicles or 24 percent of the market. Mitsubishi sold 12,486 and Nissan 12,978, giving each an 18 percent share.
